html:
Joya de Cerén is a Maya farming village in central El Salvador that was buried under volcanic ash around 600 CE. It is often called the Pompeii of the Americas.

A nearby vent, Loma Caldera, erupted without warning. The villagers fled, apparently in time, leaving their houses, tools, pots and food behind under metres of ash. Archaeologists, who found it in 1976, have uncovered houses, a sauna, storehouses and fields of maize and cassava with the plants' shapes still in the ash.

Most of what is known of the Maya comes from kings and temples; Cerén shows how farmers lived. It became a World Heritage Site in 1993. The region had already suffered from the much larger Ilopango eruption some generations before, a reminder of how volcanoes shaped El Salvador.
sum: Joya de Cerén is a Maya farming village in central El Salvador that was buried under volcanic ash around 600 CE. It is often called the Pompeii of the Americas.
